leads.summary: A failed stop or process that survives the 1-second poll still produces 'changed' and marks the migration complete
leads.consequence: If systemctl --user stop fails or an independently started fcitx5 outlives pkill, both errors are discarded, ten pgrep positives exhaust the wait, then the helper writes keyboard-fr and reports changed anyway. fcitx5 5.1.22 saves its old in-memory profile on shutdown, potentially overwriting the seed after this write. omarchy-migrate then touches the applied marker and does not retry. Recheck that no daemon is alive before writing, fail and leave the migration pending when stop cannot be completed; keep existing custom-profile guards.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus C; published as N2

leads.summary: Forced/runtime user provisioning stops a working fcitx5 daemon and does not start it again
leads.consequence: omarchy-provision-user --force (or its first runtime run without an existing finalize-user marker) sources install/user/all.sh in the graphical session. A stock US profile on a non-US vconsole causes the new helper to stop fcitx5; the install leaf only calls the helper, whereas only the migration calls omarchy-restart-xcompose. The profile becomes FR but the running session loses fcitx5 input/XCompose until a manual restart or next graphical login. If this caller stopped an active service, restore it when a graphical session exists, or make the helper return whether it stopped one so its caller can do so.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus B; published as N1

leads.summary: Conditional #9565 incompatibility: a seeded non-US profile is treated as user-customized
leads.consequence: #9565 intentionally handles untouched or previously managed groups. This PR changes an untouched Default group from us/keyboard-us to fr/keyboard-fr. When #9565's sync command is actually started, it rejects the seeded group (Default Layout != us), does not add the second engine, and tries selecting keyboard-us when Hyprland selects slot 1; fcitx5 ignores an IM absent from its group. In the opposite order, #9565 can expand a stock US group to keyboard-us + keyboard-fr while retaining DefaultIM=keyboard-us (upstream setGroup preserves it), so this helper's single-item guard exits without seeding FR and its migration still receives an applied marker. This is a verified source-level collision, conditional on #9565's new unit being installed. The currently inspected omarchy-settings PKGBUILD:178-191 does not install that new unit, so merging both without a packaging update means #9565 is already inert, not that this PR alone removes a functioning sync. Coordinate classification when that separate registration is fixed.
leads.triage: factual, coordinator-verified in pr-9565.diff sync guard and confirmed by Opus self-check; published as short related-PR note (N4), runtime interaction not claimed

leads.summary: KEYMAP-only installs permanently miss seeding if this migration runs before open XKB-exposure migrations
leads.consequence: Omarchy already acknowledges that /etc/vconsole.conf may contain KEYMAP but not XKBLAYOUT. Such an install leaves helper output empty and records migration 1790096150.sh as applied. If #11418 (1789183087.sh) or #12896 (1790044019.sh) merges after this PR and later exposes the actual non-US XKBLAYOUT, omarchy-migrate sees the existing seed marker and never revisits the stock US profile. If they ship together initially, their lower-numbered migration precedes this one and this exact order issue does not arise. Arrange a later repair/retry when XKBLAYOUT becomes available or derive a trustworthy mapping for a KEYMAP-only install.
leads.triage: factual, coordinator-verified (helper :51, omarchy-migrate:88-97, #12896 1790044019.sh, #11418 1789183087.sh); published as related-PR note (N4)

leads.summary: New shutdown regression test passes even with the process-wait block removed
leads.consequence: The active case sets FCITX_ACTIVE=0 but FCITX_PGREP=1 and the systemctl stub only logs stop, it never models the shutdown profile save or the period during which pgrep remains true. Deleting the entire wait loop leaves all 13 cases green. Add a stateful stop/pkill fixture that persists a previously loaded stock profile after a delayed shutdown, assert last disk write is FR, and check the stop failure/timeout path; include an install-leaf live-session restart assertion if fixing I2.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12920#issuecomment-5785183407) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12920#issuecomment-5841738462), checked at `f28b26521510`.

**Resolved:** the earlier finding "Stop fcitx5 before writing its new profile". [`bin/omarchy-fcitx5-seed-layout:140-154`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/f28b26521510c1b8aa547fb85585949f4473d87d/bin/omarchy-fcitx5-seed-layout#L140-L154) now stops fcitx5 before `write_profile`, and the migration restarts it afterwards when a desktop session is active. Two smaller gaps remain in the new stop path, and the new test does not check the ordering it was added for.

**Verified:** native fcitx5 5.1.22 on a private D-Bus, stock US profile, `XKBLAYOUT=fr`, with the unit and process control emulated:

| Scenario | Previous head `4552647b` | Current head `f28b2652` |
|---|---|---|
| Unit-managed fcitx5, desktop session active | keyboard-us after restart | keyboard-fr, kept after a later stop |
| fcitx5 running outside the unit, desktop session active | keyboard-us | keyboard-fr |
| No fcitx5, no session | keyboard-fr | keyboard-fr |
| No rewrite needed (already FR, or multi-IM) | fcitx5 not stopped | fcitx5 not stopped |

fcitx5 5.1.23 source keeps the same save-on-exit path (`InputMethodManager::save()` is unchanged). `systemctl --user stop` waits for the stop job, so the unit path writes only after fcitx5 has finished saving.

## Re-running the installer step leaves fcitx5 stopped

The helper now stops fcitx5, but of its two callers only [`migrations/1790096150.sh:16-18`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/f28b26521510c1b8aa547fb85585949f4473d87d/migrations/1790096150.sh#L16-L18) starts it again. [`install/user/fcitx5-layout.sh`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/f28b26521510c1b8aa547fb85585949f4473d87d/install/user/fcitx5-layout.sh) calls the helper without a restart.

```text
omarchy-provision-user --force   (from a live session, non-US console, stock US profile)
  -> install/user/all.sh -> fcitx5-layout.sh -> helper: stop fcitx5, write FR
  -> no restart: profile is FR, fcitx5 unit inactive
```

**Impact:** a manual `omarchy-provision-user --force` in a running session, when the helper has to rewrite the profile, leaves fcitx5 and its compose sequences off until the next login or `omarchy-restart-xcompose`. The first-run path is not affected because `enable-user-units.sh` starts the unit afterwards. At the previous head the same path kept fcitx5 running but lost the seed.

**Suggested change:** restart what the helper stopped when a graphical session is active, either inside the helper (and drop the migration's separate restart) or in `install/user/fcitx5-layout.sh`.

## Stop failures still report `changed`

Both stop commands end in `|| true`, and after the ten 0.1 s `pgrep` checks the helper writes the profile and prints `changed` without confirming that fcitx5 exited ([`:143-155`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/f28b26521510c1b8aa547fb85585949f4473d87d/bin/omarchy-fcitx5-seed-layout#L143-L155)). The earlier review suggested handling stop failures explicitly.

**Impact:** limited to fcitx5 running outside the unit whose shutdown save lands more than about 1 s after SIGTERM, or a stop that fails. The migration is then recorded as applied, and the late save can restore keyboard-us. This was shown only with a synthetic stand-in process, not a real slow fcitx5. The unit path is not affected. Separately, if `write_profile` fails after the stop, the migration aborts before its restart and fcitx5 stays stopped.

**Suggested change:** after the wait, exit non-zero if `pgrep -x fcitx5` still matches, so the migration stays pending and is retried. Under `omarchy-migrate`'s `set -e` this also holds back later migrations until the retry.

**Optional test improvement:** the new case in [`test/shell.d/fcitx5-layout-seed-test.sh:136-145`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/f28b26521510c1b8aa547fb85585949f4473d87d/test/shell.d/fcitx5-layout-seed-test.sh#L136-L145) checks that `stop` was called, but not that it happened before the write. A helper mutated to write first and stop afterwards (the original bug) still passes all 13 checks. Making the stop stub copy a stock US profile back over `$OMARCHY_FCITX5_PROFILE`, as fcitx5's shutdown save does, makes that mutant fail with `profile stays fr after stop-then-write` while the current head still passes.

**Related open PRs:**
- [#12896](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12896) (`1790044019.sh`) and [#11418](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/11418) (`1789183087.sh`) add `XKBLAYOUT` for installs whose `vconsole.conf` has `KEYMAP` but no `XKBLAYOUT`. This helper treats a missing `XKBLAYOUT` as US and exits without seeding, and `omarchy-migrate` still marks `1790096150.sh` applied. If this PR's migration runs on an install before either of those lands, the later `XKBLAYOUT` does not trigger a seed. Shipped together, their lower-numbered migrations run first.
- [#9565](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/9565) syncs fcitx5 with Hyprland layouts, but only adopts an untouched `Default` group with `us` / `keyboard-us`. It would not adopt or rewrite a group seeded by this PR (source reading, not run).

**Documentation:** the `omarchy-provision-user` list in `docs/file-layout.md:218-219` ("theme, chromium, git, xcompose, mise, keyring, per-user hardware quirks …") does not mention the new fcitx5 layout seed.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** follow-up limited to the stop-before-write change, its callers and the new test, plus source-level checks of related open PRs. fcitx5 5.1.22 ran natively on a private D-Bus in isolation; the systemd user unit, `pgrep` and `pkill` were emulated over fixture-owned processes. No real user manager, compositor or `graphical-session.target`; lock-screen typing was not retested. fcitx5 5.1.23 was checked by source only.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
